channel.title: QuotePlace — Quote of the Day
channel.description: One quote, every day, chosen deterministically from the QuotePlace collection.

item.title: Leo Tolstoy — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-28
item.description: “Pierre was right when he said that one must believe in the possibility of happiness in order to be happy, and I now believe in it. Let the dead bury the dead, but while I'm alive, I must live and be happy.” — Leo Tolstoy

item.title: B.R. Ambedkar — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-27
item.description: “However good a Constitution may be, it is sure to turn out bad because those who are called to work it, happen to be a bad lot.” — B.R. Ambedkar

item.title: Kamau Brathwaite — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-26
item.description: “Making with their rhythms something torn and new.” — Kamau Brathwaite

item.title: Charles Dickens — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-25
item.description: “If there were no bad people, there would be no good lawyers.” — Charles Dickens

item.title: Publilius Syrus — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-24
item.description: “Nothing can be done at once hastily and prudently.” — Publilius Syrus

item.title: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-23
item.description: “Science is the most real guide for civilisation, for life, for success in the world. To search for a guide other than science is absurdity, ignorance and heresy.” — Mustafa Kemal Atatürk

item.title: Emily Dickinson — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-22
item.description: “The pedigree of honey does not concern the bee; a clover, any time, to him is aristocracy.” — Emily Dickinson

item.title: Katherine Mansfield — Quote of the Day, 2026-11-21
item.description: “It's an infernal nuisance to love Life as I do. I seem to love it more as time goes on rather than less. It never becomes a habit to me. It's always a marvel.” — Katherine Mansfield
